reasoning_traces.think:
AFBART operates as a Bayesian ensemble of regression trees, where each tree contributes to a functional estimate of shot intensity. It leverages adaptive basis functions to capture spatial dependencies beyond fixed grid structures. The model's strength lies in its ability to perform nonparametric regression while maintaining calibrated uncertainty estimates. In GSI, this translates to robust probabilistic forecasting of 3-point and field goal outcomes. For GSE, AFBART enables dynamic state transitions based on evolving shot-diet distributions, integrating geometry-aware kernels to refine predictions in real time. The gate mechanism ensures reproducibility by requiring consistent superiority over FBART across six distinct simulation settings, validating the model’s generalization capability. The inclusion of geometry-aware bases enhances interpretability and accuracy by encoding known court layouts into the functional space. This dual role—predictive power and interpretability—makes AFBART suitable for both probabilistic inference and situational reasoning within GSE.
